newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end sharply lower on budget data.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end sharply lower on budget data.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended sharply lower on a late sell-off linked to bearish U.S. soybean production estimates included in President Bill Clinton's proposed budget, traders said.
The fiscal 1998 budget proposed for the Agriculture Department included projections for 64 million acres of soybeans to be planted this year. Production was estimated at 2.42 billion bushels.
USDA estimated 1996-97 soybean production at 2.382 billion bushels in its January 10 crop report. The next crop report is due February 12.
Soybeans ended down 9-1/2 to three cents per bushel with March down 9-1/2 at $7.30.

The market had opened firm in reaction to USDA's weekly export sales data. USDA early Thursday said U.S. net export sales of soybeans in the week ended January 30 totaled 511,900 tonnes, above expectations for 300,000 to 500,000 tonnes.
But improving growing conditions in South America and speculation Chinese demand for soybeans was weakening tempered the bullish mentality and gains were erased early.
Forecasts called for another chance of rain in Brazil's Rio Grande do Sul soybean growing regions.
Meanwhile, drier conditions prevailed in Parana where harvest was expected to begin soon.

Speculation that Chinese soybean demand was slipping further pressured the market. Chinese crush margins have collapsed recently and buyers have settled into a holiday mode for the Lunar New Year festival, trade sources there said.
Asian traders told Reuters crush margins were at or below $24 per tonne. The lower profit margins suggested diminished demand for raw materials, namely U.S. soybeans.

Bulls held onto news the USDA's agricultural attache in India cut soybean production estimates to 3.8 million tonnes from 4.03 million. The report also suggested crushers would be pushing for soybean imports with "renewed vigor."

India has been a major supplier of soymeal to Pacific Rim countries but falling crush margins have prompted a cutback in production, forcing some buyers to wait for South American supplies which should be available by March.

Funds sold at least 15 million bushels on the day. Refco Inc sold seven million bushels March and 1.5 million May. Rosenthal Collins sold four million March, Prudential Securities sold three million March and Griffin Trading sold two million March.
In options trade, Lind-Waldock sold 600 May $7.25 puts at 13-1/4 cents per bushel, traders said, and Smith Barney bought 500 May $8.00 calls and sold 500 May $7.50 calls at 8-3/4.
Soybean volume was estimated by CBOT at 50,000 contracts, above Wednesday's actual volume of 47,164 contracts.
